citations.quote: ATTACK Trial

design.text: Part A was the pivotal, randomized, assessor-blinded, comparative, noninferiority portion comparing IV SUL-DUR versus IV colistin, both with IV imipenem and cilastatin; randomization 1:1.

citations.quote: Part A was the pivotal, randomized, assessor-blinded, comparative, NI portion of the study. It compared the efficacy and safety of IV SUL-DUR versus IV colistin, both in combination with IV imipenem and cilastatin, for the treatment of subjects with ABC HABP, VABP, VP, or bacteremia.
Randomization: At a 1:1 ratio (Part A)

population.text: Subjects ≥18 years of age with HABP, VABP, VP, or bacteremia caused by Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus complex (ABC).

citations.quote: Subjects ≥18 years of age with HABP, VABP, VP, or bacteremia caused by ABC.

endpoint.text: Primary: 28-day all-cause mortality in the CRABC m-MITT population.

citations.quote: Primary: 28-day ACM in the CRABC m-MITT population;

n.text: 177 treated in Part A (randomized 181); 125 in the primary efficacy population (63 SUL-DUR, 62 colistin).

citations.quote: Part A: 177
Randomized in Part A: 181
A total of 125 subjects were assessed in the efficacy population: 63 subjects in the SUL-DUR group and 62 subjects in the colistin group.

result.text: 28-day all-cause mortality was 19.0% (12/63) with SUL-DUR vs 32.3% (20/62) with colistin; treatment difference -13.2% (95% CI -30.0, 3.5), demonstrating noninferiority within the prespecified 20% margin.

citations.quote: All-cause mortality at Day 28 was 19% (12/63) in the SUL-DUR group and 32.3% (20/62) in the colistin group, for a treatment difference (95% CI) of -13.2% (-30.0, 3.5), demonstrating that SUL-DUR was noninferior to colistin.
the primary endpoint of 28-Day all-cause mortality within the prespecified noninferiority margin of 20%.

indication.text: XACDURO is indicated in patients 18 years of age and older for the treatment of hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (HABP/VABP), caused by susceptible isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus complex.

citations.quote: XACDURO is indicated in patients 18 years of age and older for the treatment of hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (HABP/VABP), caused by susceptible isolates of *Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus* complex.

target_moa.text: Co-packaged product of sulbactam, a beta-lactam antibacterial and Ambler Class A serine beta-lactamase inhibitor that is bactericidal by inhibiting ABC penicillin-binding proteins PBP1 and PBP3, plus durlobactam, a diazabicyclooctane non-beta-lactam beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects sulbactam from degradation by certain serine-beta-lactamases.

citations.quote: Sulbactam is a beta-lactam antibacterial and Ambler Class A serine beta-lactamase inhibitor that has bactericidal activity due to its inhibition of *Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus* complex (ABC) penicillin-binding proteins PBP1 and PBP3, which are essential enzymes required for bacterial cell wall synthesis.

Durlobactam is a diazabicyclooctane non-beta-lactam, beta-lactamase inhibitor, that protects sulbactam from degradation by certain serine-beta-lactamases. Durlobactam alone does not have antibacterial activity against ABC isolates.

modality.text: Small molecule (co-packaged beta-lactam antibacterial/beta-lactamase inhibitor combination).

citations.quote: XACDURO is a co-packaged product containing sulbactam and durlobactam. Sulbactam is a beta-lactam antibacterial and Ambler Class A serine beta-lactamase inhibitor

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were liver test abnormalities (19%), diarrhea (17%), anemia (13%), and hypokalemia (12%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 40% of XACDURO patients; treatment discontinuation due to any adverse reaction in 11% (10/91). Warnings: hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) reactions and Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea.

citations.quote:
Liver test abnormalities1	17 (19)	18 (21)

Thirty-six patients (40%) in the XACDURO treatment group and 42 patients (49%) in the colistin treatment group experienced serious adverse reactions. Discontinuation of treatment due to any adverse reaction occurred in 10/91 (11%) patients treated with XACDURO
Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) reactions have been reported with beta-lactam antibacterial drugs.

requirement.text: 4452-1: Conduct a multi-dose study to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability of sulbactam-durlobactam in children from birth to less than 18 years receiving systemic antibiotic therapy (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: **4452-1:** Conduct a multi-dose study to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability of sulbactam-durlobactam in children from birth to less than 18 years who are receiving systemic antibiotic therapy for suspected or confirmed infection.

requirement.text: 4452-2: Conduct a single-arm, open-label, prospective, observational study to assess the safety of sulbactam-durlobactam, including risk of hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis), in patients with ABC complex infection.

citations.quote: **4452-2:** Conduct a single-arm, open-label, prospective, observational study to assess the safety of sulbactam-durlobactam, including the risk of hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis) in patients with *Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus* complex infection.

requirement.text: 4452-3: Conduct a mouse lymphoma TK assay (MLA) or HPRT forward mutation assay to assess the mutagenic potential of an impurity.

citations.quote: **4452-3:** Conduct a mouse lymphoma TK assay (MLA) or hypoxanthine phosphoribosyl transferase (HPRT) forward mutation assay to assess the mutagenic potential of impurity (b) (4).

requirement.text: 4452-4: Conduct a US surveillance study for a five-year period after market introduction to monitor changes in susceptibility of ABC complex organisms to sulbactam-durlobactam.

citations.quote: **4452-4:** Conduct a US surveillance study for a five-year period after the introduction of sulbactam-durlobactam to the market to monitor changes in susceptibility of *Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus* complex organisms to sulbactam-durlobactam.

requirement.text: 4452-5: Conduct studies for durlobactam drug substance and drug product to further characterize the safety of their impurity profiles and establish impurity controls in accordance with ICH Q3A, Q3B, and M7.

citations.quote: **4452-5:** Conduct studies for durlobactam drug substance and drug product, as identified in the final protocol, to further characterize the safety of their impurity profiles and establish drug substance and drug product impurity controls to ensure that each impurity limit is in accordance with ICH Q3A, Q3B, and M7, as applicable.

requirement.text: 4452-6: Complete the repeat dose toxicity study in neonatal 10-day old rats to support the planned clinical trial in children from birth to less than 1 year of age.

citations.quote: **4452-6:** Complete the repeat dose toxicity study in neonatal 10-day old rats to support the planned clinical trial in children from birth to less than 1 year of age.

requirement.text: 4452-7: Conduct studies to update the manufacturing process for each drug product component (durlobactam and sulbactam for injection) to demonstrate labeled vial content withdrawal at the lower end of fill weight variation and establish suitable controls/specifications.

citations.quote: **4452-7:** Conduct studies to update the manufacturing process for each of the drug product components (i.e., durlobactam for injection and sulbactam for injection) to demonstrate that the labeled vial content can be withdrawn at the lower end of the fill weight variation range following reconstitution

summary.text: SUL-DUR (XACDURO) was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA, received Priority Review, and was granted QIDP and Fast Track designations in 2017. It was a first cycle review, taken to the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee (12-0 favorable), and received traditional approval based on a single phase 3 noninferiority trial meeting the 28-day all-cause mortality endpoint.
